patterns_data.pattern_details: CT PPO acute hospital inpatient spend increased sharply in authorized cases. The rise reflects both more admissions and higher paid per admission, with high-acuity neuro procedures and some chemotherapy admissions visible among the drivers. This is large enough that utilization management, reimbursement, and provider review should be coordinated rather than handled as a simple volume issue.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is the single largest increase and it combines authorization exposure with inpatient reimbursement pressure.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a joint UM and network review on CT PPO authorized acute hospital admissions, prioritizing high-acuity neuro and chemotherapy cases to confirm medical necessity, level of care, and contracted payment terms.
evidence_summary: CT PPO authorized acute hospital activity added about +$23.2M, with 174 more claims and 370 more admissions.
Paid per admit increased about $4.4K and allowed per admit about $4.6K in the main CT acute hospital pocket.
Craniotomy with MCC added about +$0.9M on 10 more admissions.
Chemotherapy without acute leukemia with CC added about +$0.3M, with paid per admit up about $14.1K.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Several states show spend moving through authorization-code distribution changes or claims assigned to Not Mapped facilities. Because these records may reflect classification shifts rather than real utilization or pricing change, medical management and reimbursement action should wait until the coding and mapping are validated. The issue is most visible in CT facility mapping and in authorization-code movement in CA, WI, TX, and GA.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Without clearing these data issues first, UM and network teams risk acting on mislabeled authorization or site-of-care signals.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Have data quality and UM operations jointly validate authorization flag assignment and facility mapping logic in CA, CT, GA, KY, TX, VA, and WI, then restate the affected inpatient trend before policy or contract changes.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Spend is concentrated in claims flagged for authorization-code distribution shifts or Not Mapped facility values, so the signal may reflect coding or mapping movement rather than true business change.
evidence_summary: CT PPO authorized claims in Not Mapped facilities account for about +$4.7M, with 56 more admissions and paid per admit up about $30.5K.
Authorization-code distribution shifts expose about +$1.3M in CA, +$1.1M in WI, and +$0.5M in TX before true business action can be set.
KY HMO Not Mapped facility spend adds about +$1.1M, and smaller Not Mapped pockets also appear in CA, VA, and WI.
All authorization-code groups are explicitly flagged for validation before action.

These should be managed as catastrophic case review and complex tertiary-care contracting, not as a general inpatient trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A small number of catastrophic cases can materially move spend and require different clinical and financial action than broad utilization growth.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Route these CA cases for catastrophic case review, confirm diagnosis and procedure coding, and assess whether complex tertiary-case contracting and outlier protections are adequate.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern is driven by rare, small-number, high-cost cases, so chart-level confirmation is needed before broader action.
evidence_summary: CA rare high-cost clinical findings total about +$5.5M across two related case-mix clusters.

Other craniotomy diagnoses added about +$0.8M and +$0.7M, each on only 4 to 8 admissions.
A separate CA neuro intensity signal added about +$1.0M on 4 admissions, with paid per admit about $60.9K.
